title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 163 (Bailor entitled to increase or profit from goods bailed)

content.overview: Section 163 provides that in the absence of any contract to the contrary, the bailee is bound to deliver to the bailor, or according to his directions, any increase or profit which may have accrued from the goods bailed.
content.glance: Absent a contrary contract, the bailee must deliver to the bailor any increase or profit accruing from the goods bailed.
content.study: In the absence of any contract to the contrary, the bailee is bound to deliver to the bailor, or according to his directions, any increase or profit which may have accrued from the goods bailed. Current-law framing: accretions and profits belong to the bailor unless the contract provides otherwise.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: In the absence of any contract to the contrary, the bailee is bound to deliver to the bailor, or according to his directions, any increase or profit which may have accrued from the goods bailed.

examples.title: Offspring of bailed animal
examples.body: Absent contrary contract, any increase (such as offspring) or profit from bailed goods must be delivered to the bailor under Section 163.

hypotheticals.question: Goods bailed produce an increase. Who is entitled to it absent a contrary contract?
hypotheticals.analysis: The bailor, under Section 163; the bailee must deliver it according to directions.
